name: Bianca Cole
life: “My old cleaning partner could identify every crane crew by its sandwich crumbs.” People around Breakwater Way know Bianca by a small Thursday habit. Bianca stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I was asked to throw them away. I put a forwarding card in each one instead.
appearance: Bianca is easy to recognize by black hair twisted into a small knot and a long face and high cheekbones. Usually dressed in a soft blue checked shirt with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead, Bianca looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Bianca always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Bianca is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To attach forwarding tags to the uncollected containers.
family: Chris Anders is Bianca’s cousin. Bianca puts the kettle on. Chris chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *Rent in a biscuit tin*, Chris says, “I was sure my envelope had been opened. The crease was mine from the night I nearly spent it.”
connections: Vincent Farah. They make sure the whale lid goes into the correct forwarding bag. Also in the story is Logan Calder (roster planner).

reactions.response: Bianca puts the unclaimed tin by for a later handover.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Bianca asks which name they want to hear next time and uses it in the next ordinary introduction.
